meta.title: Tesla, Priced for the Robots
meta.dek: Since its 2021 peak Tesla's revenue has nearly doubled, its operating profit has fallen by a third and its stock has gone nowhere. Now Musk wants to fold it into SpaceX. What does $374 assume, and who gets paid if the merger happens?
meta.price_note: Oct 21, 2026 close; $373.63 after hours on the Q3 print
meta.type: Auto OEM and energy storage carrying an autonomy, robotics and AI-compute option

verdict.sentence: Tesla's car business earns little and its autonomy business is real but undisclosed; at $386 the price assumes more than my Bull, and the probability-weighted case, merger premium included, is worth about [[pw_ev]].
verdict.breaks_if: Tesla discloses robotaxi economics at Tesla's own ~$0.30-a-mile cost target with a fleet growing toward 100,000 vehicles, or the SpaceX committees agree a premium above 20% for Tesla holders.
verdict.moat: Narrow, narrowing in autos; optional Wide in autonomy
verdict.next: NHTSA reply Oct 30; ACEA Sep data; meeting Dec 3
verdict.compounding: [[Base.cagr]] EPS from a trough, but the multiple falls ~9×

call: Tesla has become two companies with one share price. The first builds cars and batteries: Q3 revenue was flat at $28.0B, auto gross margin ex-credits recovered to 18.1%, and the operating margin was 2.6%, while BYD outsold Tesla in the EU this year. The second is an autonomy and robotics company: 1.74M paid FSD customers, nearly two million cumulative unsupervised robotaxi miles and an Optimus line now producing. It has still not disclosed a fleet size, a cost per mile or a revenue line. Q3 was a good quarter for cash: free cash flow was +$1.5B, cash and investments reached $45.4B ($35.9B net of debt), and 2026 capex was cut to about $20B. None of that changes what the price needs. At $386 the stock needs FY2031 EPS near [[Priced-in.eps]] to earn 10% a year, above my Bull's [[Bull.eps]]. The probability-weighted case, including Optimus at scale (10%) and a SpaceX merger premium (65%), is worth about [[pw_ev]]: [[pw_return]] a year. Price-implied Bear odds are below zero; R/R is [[rr]].

tests.if_fail: move 10 points from Bull to Bear (PW EV [[test1.pw_ev]], [[test1.pw_return]]/yr) → stays **[[test1.verb]] / Trim**, entry [[test1.entry]]; the autonomy case loses its evidence.

tests.claim: That Optimus is production, not a press cycle.
tests.test: a unit count or weekly run-rate in the Q4 update (late January 2027). Q3 confirmed production on Fremont's high-volume lines but gave no count; Musk put 20,000 a week at least a year away.
tests.if_fail: the Optimus option falls to 5% (PW EV [[t2_pw]], [[t2_ret]]/yr) → stays **Watch / Trim**, entry [[t2_entry]].

tests.claim: That Europe is a model-year gap, not brand damage.
tests.test: ACEA EU registrations for September through December (late October to late January) back above the prior year, with Tesla ahead of BYD in at least one month.
tests.if_fail: move 10 points from Base to Bear (PW EV [[test3.pw_ev]], [[test3.pw_return]]/yr) → stays **Watch / Trim**, entry [[test3.entry]].

return_math.compounding: Base GAAP EPS grows [[Base.cagr]] a year from a trough of [[Base.eps0]] to [[Base.eps]], but the multiple falls from about 425× to 50×, so the Base returns [[Base.return]] a year. No dividend, no buyback, about 1% a year dilution. Every case loses money at a flat multiple path because today's multiple is not one any case can hold.
return_math.price_implied: At 10% and a 50× exit, spot needs FY2031 EPS of about [[Priced-in.eps]] ([[Priced-in.cagr]] a year), above the Bull's [[Bull.eps]]; at 13% it needs about [[Hurdle.eps]]. The price assumes Musk's robotaxi and robot plans largely arrive on time.
return_math.epv: About $34 a share: five-year average owner earnings of about $8.4B capitalized at 10% (≈$24) plus net cash of about $10 a share ex-leases. About 90% of the price pays for growth. The Bear ([[Bear.value]]) sits well above EPV because it keeps storage and autonomy growing.
return_math.base_rate: The Bull grows revenue about 19% a year from $107B; under 5% of companies above $50B have grown 15% a year in real terms for five years, so the Bull is plausible only on autonomy. The Base's 10% a year sits near the top decile, carried by storage and autonomy.
return_math.year_ten: In the Bull and Base, autonomy is still growing at year ten; the 50× exit assumes it. In the Bear the multiple does the work.
return_math.terminal_growth: Implied perpetual growth at 10%: Bull [[Bull.g]], Base [[Base.g]], Bear [[Bear.g]], all above the 5.15% Treasury. A 50× exit is only defensible for a business still compounding above 20% in 2031; I accept the flag for the Bull and Base and note that the Bear's 27× is generous.
return_math.note: Computed rows come from model.json; EPV, base rate, year ten and the terminal-growth reading are the author's. Built with Claude.
